<!-- pr-reviewer: 8f1f470355c81fa7e78aac8c816d83aa6f0ed327 -->
Review (Opus): blockers

Independent read-only review of head `8f1f470355c81fa7e78aac8c816d83aa6f0ed327`. The head contains `origin/main`, and `git merge-tree` with `origin/main` is clean.

## Blocker

1. **The pin reuses the temp directory pattern that #3290 removed.** `a_crashed_step_executable_says_how_it_stopped_in_its_log_and_note` uses `temp_dir().join(format!("camcraft-xtask-3258-{}", process::id()))`, then `create_dir_all`, then `File::create`. This is the `bore_core` defect of uma (44987903117). On a host with a shared `/tmp` and more than one runner account, a leftover directory of a different account with the same PID makes `create_dir_all` pass and `File::create` fail with `PermissionDenied`. The xtask unit tests run in the post-merge batch tier on the same hosts. The PR says that this pattern caused one of the #3258 faults, so the new test must not add it again. Fix: reserve the directory with an atomic `create_dir` and skip `AlreadyExists`, as `fixture_dir` in `crates/app/tests/bore_core.rs` does.

## Root cause (step 1)

- skull (44948384882) and egg (44950073227): the evidence is good. The kernel logs show a segfault in `libvulkan.so` at the failure time, and the tests that did not finish are the GPU tests. I read the egg log: `FAIL in 1s exit -1` on `ui suites: trace_parity`.
- wopr (44955923206): the evidence is weaker. mkinney wrote that the wopr kernel log has "no kernel segfault, no OOM", and that wopr matches the overlap hypothesis. The PR body and the decision file do not say this. They put wopr under the driver cause only because the run ended before the 22:40Z pin. Add the wopr facts to the decision file: which Vulkan driver wopr used before the pin, and why the driver is the cause when no segfault is in the log.
- After the pin: I counted 27 post-merge runs since 22:40Z (12 success, 11 failure, 3 cancelled, 1 in progress). I read the FAIL rows of the 11 red runs. 10 are `slot_dxf_sketch` and 1 is `example_catalog`. None is a UI `exit -1`. This agrees with the PR.
- uma `bore_core` (44987903117): #3290 explains it. I agree.
- Not explained:
  - skull 44982953354: the batch gate hung for 63 min and was cancelled. No log is available.
  - uma 44995766211, attempt 1 (06:53-07:07Z): the job annotation is "The self-hosted runner lost communication with the server". The "Batch gate tier" step has no end time, and the job has no log. Attempt 2 runs on uma now.
  - These two faults are runner-level stops, not a test executable that a signal kills. The new line does not show them, because the gate writes no summary when the runner stops.

**Fixes or Refs.** The title of #3258 is the UI abort signature, and the PR explains that signature with evidence (wopr with the gap above). Thus `Fixes #3258` is acceptable on one condition. Before the merge, file a `source:agent` follow-up issue for the runner-level stops (44982953354 and 44995766211 attempt 1), and name it in the PR body. If no follow-up is filed, use `Refs #3258`.

## Code (step 2)

- Unix: the signal numbers 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13 and 15 are the same on Linux and macOS. SIGBUS is correctly left out, because its number is not portable. `ExitStatusExt::signal` and `core_dumped` are used only inside `#[cfg(unix)]`. The Unix test is `#[cfg(unix)]`. `ExitStatus::from_raw(11 | 0x80)` is the correct raw wait status for SIGSEGV with a core dump. I did not build on Unix.
- Windows: `0xC0000005`, `0xC000001D`, `0xC00000FD`, `0xC0000409`, `0xC000013A` and `0xC0000142` are correct NTSTATUS values. Suggestion (not a blocker): add `0xC0000135` (a DLL was not found), `0xC0000374` (heap corruption) and `0xC0000094` (integer divide by zero). A test executable on Windows can stop on these statuses.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside the tests. Errors of the new `writeln!` go through `map_err(io)`.
- Parsers: `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` takes the rows that match `^ +FAIL `, and it gets the suites from `tests/<name>.rs` in the note. The new note adds text after `exit -1` and adds no `tests/` text, so the parser and the P1/P2 choice do not change. The `exit {code}` note in `known_fail_tests.rs` is a test input only. No other code reads the `exit -1` note.
- Note (not a blocker): in a direct step with more than one executable, if one executable has `test result: FAILED`, the note shows that list and not the signal. The signal line is still in the step log.

## Tests (step 3)

- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask exit_status` on Windows, in a detached worktree of the head (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `-j 6`): 4 passed, 0 failed.
- Mutation: I put back the `direct.rs` of the parent commit. The pin failed with `no stop line in: Running crash (cmd)`. The other 3 tests passed. With the PR code, the pin passes. I removed the worktree.
- Not run: the Unix test and the Unix branch of the pin. No Unix build was made.

## Process (step 4)

- The body has `Process change: yes`. The PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.
- `docs/decisions/3258-gate-names-the-crash.md` has the correct format: a `## #3258 - ...` heading, what was decided, why, what was dropped and the cost to change later.
- The body has `Changelog: none` and `Fixes #3258`.

No label was changed. The PR stays a draft.

Delta re-check (Opus): clean

Read-only re-check of the delta `8f1f47035..1abbab1c4` (one commit: `fix(xtask): reserve the pin's temp dir atomically; add three crash statuses`).

- **Temp directory (the blocker of the last review): fixed.** The pin now reserves its directory with `std::fs::create_dir`. This call is one atomic `mkdir` and it does not succeed on a directory that exists. A leftover directory of a different runner account gives `AlreadyExists`, and the loop then tries the next number. No race is possible between the check and the create, because the create is the check. Errors other than `AlreadyExists` panic with the path. This is permitted in a test. The loop stops after 1000 tries with `expect`, so it cannot hang.
- **NTSTATUS codes: correct.** `0xC0000094` is STATUS_INTEGER_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO. `0xC0000135` is STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND. `0xC0000374` is STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION. The Windows test now also pins `0xC0000374`.
- **wopr:** the decision file and the body now say that mkinney found no kernel segfault and no OOM on wopr, and that the wopr abort is attributed to the driver by its time only.
- **Follow-up:** the body names #3303 (open, P3, `source:agent`) for the two runner-level stops (44982953354 and 44995766211 attempt 1). Thus `Fixes #3258` is correct.
- **Tests:** `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask exit_status` on Windows, in a detached worktree of `1abbab1c4` (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `-j 6`): 4 passed, 0 failed. I removed the worktree. The Unix branch was not built.

No label was changed.

Coordinator: this PR is xtask-only (a process change). It merges when it is reviewed (AGENTS.md). The reviews that this merge relies on are the Opus review (comment 7075899808) and its clean delta re-check on head 1abbab1c4 (comment 7075926555). The quick gate is green on 8f1f47035. On this head, `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask exit_status` passes 4 of 4 and clippy on xtask is green. The Unix branch first runs on the post-merge runner. I flag it ready and merge it on head 1abbab1c4. Nothing is pushed after this flag. A `PROCESS_VERSION` bump follows.
